neuro-autoresearch report

10 run/study file(s) · 474 attempt(s) · 67 failed (14%) · 93 omitted from plots · datasets: NsdSubj01

What the search found

This loop evolves a hand-written, never-trained feature extractor (model.py): a stimulus image is mapped to features, a ridge readout is fit against recorded fMRI (the only thing fit — that fit is the evaluation), and held-out test_corr on NSD subject 01 is the reward. Each run rewards a single visual region, and the report compares the winner to both the logged identity/raw-pixel baseline and the documented trained-AlexNet reference.

The architecture the search converged on (in every region). Without being told to, the loop rediscovered the classical early-visual front-end:

  • Quadrature Gabor banks (orientations × spatial wavelengths) reduced to complex-cell energy √(cos² + sin²) — V1 simple→complex cells;
  • colour opponency (luminance, R−G, B−Y) — retinal/LGN channels;
  • log contrast compression followed by divisive normalization with a spatial-surround pool — Heeger's canonical cortical gain control;
  • raw pixels concatenated in as a low-level anchor.

On top of this shared core, each region added a distinct elaboration: a second scattering layer (Gabor-on-energy) for V2/V3, a wider normalization pool for V3's larger receptive fields, texture Gram matrices + GIST + random Fourier features for scene-selective PPA, colour histograms for EBA, and heterogeneous random conv banks for the face/word regions.

Key findings.

  1. V1 is the most predictable region and the simplest model wins it — a pure Gabor-energy model with a 3×3 surround norm. Predictivity then falls along the cortical hierarchy V1 > V2 > V3 > hV4 > category-selective regions.
  2. Every region's best model still predicts V1 best (~0.40 in the column below, regardless of which region was the reward). The region-specific machinery buys only modest gains on its own target — the models remain fundamentally low-level/V1-like and do not yet capture high-level category selectivity (FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA stay ≈0.20–0.29).
  3. The baseline chart makes the main boundary clear: untrained encoders can match or beat AlexNet in early/mid visual cortex, but still trail the learned network in high-level category regions where semantics matter.

Computational principles

Each run proposes fixed feature extractors, then the ridge readout asks: which hand-written computation makes brain activity easier to predict? The bars below sum the reward gains from improving steps that mention each principle. A single step can count for multiple principles because real models combine ingredients.

  • Gabor / oriented energy — quadrature filter pairs collapsed to √(cos²+sin²) give phase-invariant edge/contrast detectors (V1 complex cells).
  • Divisive normalization — dividing each unit by a pooled neighbourhood is the canonical cortical gain-control that decorrelates and equalises contrast (Heeger).
  • Colour opponency — luminance / R−G / B−Y channels mirror retinal–LGN coding.
  • Multiscale / spatial frequency — a bank of wavelengths covers coarse layout through fine detail; different regions weight the bands differently.
  • Scattering / second order — a Gabor layer applied to the first layer's energy captures the nonlinear pooling V2/V3 perform on V1 output (translation-stable).
  • Texture statistics — Gram / GIST / Portilla–Simoncelli summaries describe material and scene structure, which drives PPA and the ventral stream.
  • Random features — fixed random projections (RFF, random convs, codebooks) lift features into a high-dimensional kernel space without any training.
  • Pooling / retinotopy — foveal weighting and spatial grids encode where things are, not just what.

The search process

How did the search actually progress? These views read the ledger's iterations, reward values, train–test gap, and status field to characterize the search dynamics rather than any single model.

  • Progress — best reward as a function of iteration, or wall-clock when reliable seconds are present.
  • Failure rate — non-ok status rows as a percentage of all iterations.
  • Generalization gap — train_corr − test_corr tracks how much the ridge readout overfits as features grow richer.
  • Iteration accounting — scored rows versus failed rows when compute timing is not available in the report data.

Cross-region predictivity

Each row is the best model found for one reward region; each column is a brain region scored after the same ridge readout. This makes it easier to see whether a model is genuinely region-specific or mostly predicts early visual cortex.

Rows: each run's best model. Columns: the region it is scored against. Note how the V1 column stays high across every run.

Model mechanics — what each run's best model computes

Cards are ordered by reward. Each card names the target brain region, describes the computation directly, and includes source code when the original run folder is available.

V1 run — best model for primary visual cortex (V1) test_corr 0.4278

gabor-lum-surround · identity 0.3065 · AlexNet 0.3420

Idea. Replace per-pixel divnorm with V1's spatial-surround normalization (cross-channel energy pooled over a 3x3 neighborhood before dividing), the canonical normalization pool.

Computation. Raw RGB pixels + log-compressed (gain 100) full-resolution complex-cell energy maps from an 8-orientation x 5-wavelength (1.5-7.5px) quadrature Gabor bank on luminance, divisively normalized by a 3x3 spatial-surround cross-channel pool.

across regions: V1=0.43 · hV4=0.26 · early=0.31 · ventral=0.23 · PPA=0.23 · EBA=0.21 · FFA=0.20 · VWFA=0.15

V2 run — best model for secondary visual cortex (V2) test_corr 0.3710

gabor-color-dog-scatter3c · AlexNet 0.2990

Idea. The luminance-only full-res scatter is the best (0.3708); extend the 2nd layer to all 3 opponent channels at FULL resolution (4-orient L2 bank, no pre-pool) to add color-contingent contour combinations while keeping the spatial detail that coarse pre-pooling lost.

Computation. Best fft model PLUS a full-resolution 2nd scattering layer: 4-orient x 2-scale Gabor energy on the scale-summed L1-energy orientation maps of all 3 opponent channels, avg-pooled to 4x4; rank->normal Gaussianized.

across regions: V1=0.44 · V2=0.37 · V3=0.36 · hV4=0.29 · early=0.33 · ventral=0.26 · PPA=0.26 · EBA=0.26 · FFA=0.24 · VWFA=0.18

V3 run — best model for visual area V3 test_corr 0.3498

gabor-v3-tunednorm · AlexNet 0.3210

Idea. Replace untuned all-channel divisive normalization with orientation-tuned cross-orientation suppression: normalize each orientation channel by the 7x7-pooled energy summed over OTHER orientations at the same scale/color, the classic V1/V2/V3 mechanism that sharpens orientation contrast.

Computation. Raw pixels + log(gain 300) full-res 12-ori x 5-wl color complex-cell energy, normalized by a 7x7-pooled cross-orientation (same scale/color) energy sum (tuned normalization). Never trained.

across regions: V1=0.44 · V2=0.37 · V3=0.35 · hV4=0.28 · early=0.32 · ventral=0.25 · PPA=0.24 · EBA=0.23 · FFA=0.22 · VWFA=0.16

EBA run — best model for body-selective area (EBA) test_corr 0.2901

colorhist_chroma · identity 0.1449 · AlexNet 0.4360

Idea. Add a complementary substrate orthogonal to oriented energy: nonlinear color-appearance features (soft RBF assignment of each pixel to a fixed color codebook, spatially pooled = regional color histograms) for skin/scene cues EBA responds to.

Computation. Chromatic Gabor energy pyramid + color + spatial color-histogram features (RBF soft-assignment to a 64-color codebook), standardized; 48000 ReLU conjunctions + luminance-invariant chromaticity histogram.

across regions: V1=0.40 · hV4=0.27 · early=0.30 · ventral=0.24 · PPA=0.28 · EBA=0.29 · FFA=0.27 · VWFA=0.19

hV4 run — best model for color/shape area hV4 test_corr 0.2819

ranknorm-rich9s · identity 0.1510 · AlexNet 0.2890

Idea. Divisive normalization is the canonical cortical computation (Heeger): normalize each orientation's complex-cell energy by the pooled local energy across orientations+space to get contrast-invariant, tuning-sharpened responses that match V4 better than raw energy, plus HMAX max-pooling for position invariance.

Computation. Opponent (lum,R-G,B-Y) Gabor energy (3sc x 8ori); divisively normalized by local cross-orientation energy (blur pool) + semisaturation; both raw and normalized energy multi-pooled (4,2,1) and concatenated with block color.

across regions: V1=0.42 · hV4=0.28 · early=0.31 · ventral=0.25 · PPA=0.27 · EBA=0.27 · FFA=0.25 · VWFA=0.18

PPA run — best model for place/scene area (PPA) test_corr 0.2669

gist_rff_tex2hf · identity 0.1460 · AlexNet 0.4030

Idea. Add a fine high-spatial-frequency Gabor scale (ks=5, lambda=2) to the proven gist_rff_tex2 bank: PPA is documented to prefer high SF and rectilinear/high-detail structure, but every existing scale is coarse (lambda>=3) on the 16x16 input, so the high-SF band that drives PPA is currently missing.

Computation. gist_rff_tex2 (color divnorm GIST + 4-bandwidth RFF + global/2x2 cross-orientation texture Gram) with an added fine high-SF Gabor scale (ks=5,sigma=1.0,lambda=2.0), contributing both GIST energy and texture-Gram features at the high-frequency band.

across regions: V1=0.37 · hV4=0.24 · early=0.28 · ventral=0.20 · PPA=0.27 · EBA=0.25 · FFA=0.23 · VWFA=0.16

FFA run #2 — best model for face-selective area (FFA) test_corr 0.2613

spatial_moments_v90 · AlexNet 0.3960

Idea. Continue the compression-exponent trend (0.5->0.4 helped): test p=0.33 (cube-root) for even stronger low-contrast emphasis, a budget-neutral tweak to find the optimum, on v85.

Computation. v13 ensemble + 2nd-order scattering: 32 S1 Gabor-energy maps each re-filtered by a 6-orient quadrature bank (grouped conv) to a modulus, 4x4-pooled (~3k extra); ~15k-d.

across regions: V1=0.40 · hV4=0.26 · early=0.30 · ventral=0.23 · PPA=0.28 · EBA=0.29 · FFA=0.26 · VWFA=0.18

ventral run — best model for ventral visual stream test_corr 0.2587

10ori+fullcross2 · AlexNet 0.2840

Idea. Add a compact luminance cross-scale x orientation co-occurrence Gram (richer contour/part co-occurrence than texstat's adjacent-summed scales) to the proven base, and chunk the rank-normalization over columns so the large feature matrix never spikes GPU memory -- making the strongest model both richer and robust on the shared GPU.

Computation. rich9s opponent Gabor energy (divisive norm + multi-pool) + orientation/cross-scale Gram + PS marginals + scale-x-color and luminance scale-x-12-orientation energy co-occurrence Grams; whole concatenation rank->normal transformed in memory-safe column chunks.

across regions: V1=0.42 · hV4=0.29 · early=0.31 · ventral=0.26 · PPA=0.28 · EBA=0.29 · FFA=0.26 · VWFA=0.19

FFA run #1 — best model for face-selective area (FFA) test_corr 0.2439

hetero-convbank · identity 0.1290 · AlexNet 0.3960

Idea. Complementary fixed feature families should out-predict a single random bank: random 3/5/7 filters (local texture), dilated random filters (larger receptive field for global face layout), and oriented Gabors (V1-like edges) jointly span more of FFA's stimulus structure than any one alone.

Computation. Fixed banks over the 0.5-centered RGB image -- random 3/5/7 convs, dilated (d=2,3) random 3x3 convs, and an 8-orientation x 3-freq x 2-phase Gabor bank -- each ReLU'd then avg+max pooled on 1x1/2x2/3x3 grids; raw, never trained.

across regions: V1=0.39 · hV4=0.25 · early=0.29 · ventral=0.22 · PPA=0.27 · EBA=0.26 · FFA=0.24 · VWFA=0.18

VWFA run — best model for visual word-form area (VWFA) test_corr 0.1952

convbank+gisttex+xscale+fovea+v1dense · identity 0.1051 · AlexNet 0.3210

Idea. Complementarity is the only thing that ever moved VWFA (0.18->0.194); merge the V1-winning representation I have never combined -- dense, full-resolution, position-PRESERVING surround-normalized complex-cell energy (8 orient x 5 wavelength) -- which retains spatial layout my pooled position-invariant branches discard, a genuinely different family.

Computation. Branches: random+Gabor conv banks (avg+max pool); GIST + Gram + cross-scale corr; compact foveal energy; PLUS dense 16x16 surround-normalized log-compressed Gabor energy (V1-style, position-preserving). Concatenated, each standardized, never trained.

across regions: V1=0.43 · hV4=0.28 · early=0.32 · ventral=0.25 · PPA=0.29 · EBA=0.29 · FFA=0.26 · VWFA=0.20
